statement: Summary models no-adaptation annual losses at 3-4% GDP by 2030 and 9.4% by 2050; over two million people could fall into poverty by mid-century.
compact_statement: Summary models no-adaptation annual losses at 3-4% GDP by 2030 and 9.4% by 2050; over two million people could fall into poverty by mid-century.

source_refs.locator: Executive Summary, printed p. 1 (PDF p. 4), modeled cost of inaction.

statement: Selected-sector adaptation could add about 2% GDP by 2030 and reduce climate-induced poverty by 45% versus no action.
compact_statement: Selected-sector adaptation could add about 2% GDP by 2030 and reduce climate-induced poverty by 45% versus no action.
scenario: Selected adaptation versus no action; assumptions unstated.

source_refs.locator: Executive Summary, printed p. 1 (PDF p. 4), adaptation scenario results.

statement: Half of Senegal's population and two-thirds of GDP face sea-level exposure; Dakar's population at coastal-flood risk is projected to rise 20-30% by 2050.
compact_statement: Half of Senegal's population and two-thirds of GDP face sea-level exposure; Dakar's population at coastal-flood risk is projected to rise 20-30% by 2050.

source_refs.locator: Executive Summary, printed p. 2 (PDF p. 6), coastal exposure.

uncertainty: National exposure and Dakar change; no district detail.

statement: The diagnostic reports that the 2002 drought reduced agricultural production by about 35% and the 2011 drought by 20%; estimated production losses across 12 major crops during 1980–2020 totaled FCFA 852 billion, averaging 3.9% of agricultural GDP annually.
compact_statement: The diagnostic reports that the 2002 drought reduced agricultural production by about 35% and the 2011 drought by 20%; estimated production losses across 12 major crops during 1980–2020 totaled FCFA 852 billion, averaging 3.9% of agricultural GDP annually.

source_refs.locator: Section 3.2.2, printed p. 20 (PDF p. 21), historical drought impacts on agriculture and food security.

uncertainty: Historical estimates combine reported episodes and statistical analysis across 12 crops; the report notes modeled risk robustness depends on input data.

statement: The diagnostic says northern Senegal is projected to experience more frequent extreme droughts, particularly in Saint-Louis; its cited CCDR scenarios estimate annual GDP losses of 3.6–4% by 2030 and 7–9.4% by 2050 without adaptation.
compact_statement: The diagnostic says northern Senegal is projected to experience more frequent extreme droughts, particularly in Saint-Louis; its cited CCDR scenarios estimate annual GDP losses of 3.6–4% by 2030 and 7–9.4% by 2050 without adaptation.
scenario: Climate projections for northern drought; cited CCDR GDP range varies by warming assumption and assumes no adaptation.

source_refs.locator: Section 3.7, printed p. 28 (PDF p. 29), forward climate-risk analysis.

uncertainty: GDP figures are from the separate Senegal CCDR, cited by this diagnostic; they are not observed losses.

statement: Senegal’s NDC reports declining rainfall, rising mean temperature, sea-level rise, and disruptions to cultivable land, water, and fisheries; it identifies northern regions, especially Saint-Louis, as facing a 20–30% increase in extreme-drought frequency, and identifies more wet extremes in Matam, Tambacounda, and Louga under its low-warming scenario.
compact_statement: Senegal’s NDC reports declining rainfall, rising mean temperature, sea-level rise, and disruptions to cultivable land, water, and fisheries; it identifies northern regions, especially Saint-Louis, as facing a 20–30% increase in extreme-drought frequency, and identifies more wet extremes in Matam, Tambacounda, and Louga under its low-warming scenario.
affected_groups: People whose livelihoods depend on natural resources
scenario: NDC low-warming scenario for wet extremes; drought-frequency scenario is not further labeled in the cited summary.

source_refs.locator: Section I, printed p. 3 (PDF p. 3), observed impacts and climate-risk projections.

uncertainty: This is a 2020 NDC projection; the summarized model passage does not name an RCP/SSP or projection year.
